trends.title: Bottlenecks move, they do not disappear
trends.lastLog: Held (0.80) · the newly registered dedicated class A entered its first observation period, 0/3 this week; but one high-quality "new layer" candidate reading appeared · The dedicated class A for this trend was newly registered by ruling on 2026-08-26, and requires that, before the lock point (2027-06), there appear ≥3 readings from independent primary sources each recording a supply shortage that has already occurred in a non-HBM component; each reading must fall after the 2026-08-26 registration date and must be the first threshold crossing for that component in the current round of tightness (the component must not already have been in shortage in the 12 months before the reading date). Zero readings counted this week; the exclusions, one by one: ① memory spot fill rate fell below 50%, 16Gb DDR4 +879% YoY, entering allocation (BoA, 27 Aug) — DDR4/NAND is literally a "non-HBM component", but the category was already in shortage in the 12 months before the reading date and so fails the "first threshold crossing" test; ② transformer and grid equipment lead times (a US emergency declaration blocking foreign equipment from entering) — already priced in at T06 / C39, and likewise not a first crossing; ③ Fujifilm tripling post-CMP cleaning fluid capacity — that is capacity expansion, not a shortage reading. ⚡ But this week produced the closest thing yet, for this trend, to a wave migrating to a new layer: two independent sources report that within the thermal domain the bottleneck has moved from "can it be liquid-cooled" to CDUs, pumps, hoses and on-site commissioning crews — "a project can have land, GPUs and financing at once and still be stuck on grid connection or a transformer; fix one constraint and the next long-lead-time item becomes the new critical path" (r/datacenter, 27-28 Aug). This is a literal reprise of the trend's underlying mechanism, but the evidence sits entirely at the leading-indicator layer, and on its own this is not enough to count as a class A reading; registered for observation: if any further search next week gives an event-level reading on CDU or pump lead times, allocation or book-to-bill, that constitutes the first class A entry. A second candidate from the same source is "the speed at which human experience is formed" (skilled electricians and commissioning crews), registered in the capability-surplus evolution log on 2026-08-15 and surfacing again this week (data centre pay is draining municipal public-sector electricians, while union electricians and apprentices explicitly refuse projects)
trends.oneliner: AI infrastructure bottlenecks are never eliminated, only pushed into the adjacent layer (GPU→HBM→packaging→interconnect→passive components→materials→power→water/permitting/skilled labour); each layer that is unblocked transfers the pressure to the weakest layer next to it.
trends.mechanism: TOC (Theory of Constraints) + throughput in a series system is set by its weakest node. When capital floods in to expand capacity at one node, adjacent nodes cannot expand in proportion, so the constraint necessarily migrates. The further down the chain, the closer to physical, geological and permitting cycles, and the smaller the elasticity of capacity expansion.
trends.analogy: The narrowest cross-section in fluid mechanics: the thinnest point of a pipe sets the flow; widen one section and the next narrow section immediately becomes the new bottleneck. Similar to a series circuit, whose total impedance is always dominated by the largest single element.

trends.title: Memory and bandwidth become the main constraint
trends.lastLog: Strengthened 0.82→0.84 · the memory axis is read directly off a buyer's cost structure for the first time: NVDA's FY27Q2 supply-chain commitments run US$119bn→US$279bn, HBM spending exceeds the wafers themselves, and within procurement cost SK hynix 27% + Micron 14% = 41% now exceeds TSMC's 37% (primary-source earnings report, 26 Aug); BoA channel checks put the memory spot fill rate below 50% and 16Gb DDR4 spot prices +879% YoY; NVDA raised full-system prices 15-17%, explicitly passing memory costs through, and 2027 HBM contract prices are expected to rise 70-140%. |Δp|=0.02 [Q1]. ⚠️ Set against this, four "de-HBM" paths emerged in the same week (d-Matrix Raptor / Qualcomm HBC / Jalapeño HBM4+SRAM fusion / Samsung LPDDR5X-PIM) plus a 4.44× reduction in KV cache on the architecture side — all four still sit inside the memory axis, which is precisely what validates the need for the 22 Aug axis-level rewrite of the class A criterion; rechecked against the 15 Aug effect criterion, the class B tripwire is still judged not to have been hit; class A came closest to a hit but collapse was refused because a supplier's own cost split ≠ an independent institution's BOM teardown, and only one company is involved
trends.oneliner: AI inference spends 90% of its time moving weights; HBM has been promoted from a cyclical commodity to a strategic asset, the valuation paradigm has switched from P/B to P/E, and long-term contracts (LTAs) lock in 3-5 years of capacity.
trends.mechanism: Compute grows at ~59%/year against memory bandwidth at ~23%/year, a gap compounded over 30+ years; the energy cost of moving data is close to a thousand times that of computing on it; the very low arithmetic intensity of inference leaves GPUs stalled on memory bandwidth. DRAM/HBM capacity expansion has a hard cycle of ≥ 2 years while AI inference demand is close to unbounded → a mismatch in the time constants of supply and demand elasticity → the price curve turns from cyclical to structural.
trends.analogy: 19th-century railways: once locomotive power rose, the bottleneck shifted to gauge, signalling and scheduling systems, and value moved from locomotive builders to network operators. Lithium mining for electric vehicles: demand doubles year on year but opening a mine takes 5-7 years.

trends.title: Advanced packaging defines compute
trends.lastLog: Strengthened 0.82→0.84 · the claim that packaging allocation directly defines compute output gets its first named, quantified evidence: constrained by packaging supply, Broadcom's expected total 2026 CoWoS output has been lowered from 250,000 wafers to 215,000, which translates directly into a 32,000-wafer cut in Google's TPU v7x allocation ≈ 500,000 chips, with v8i lowered in step; in 2027 Meta's MTIA 400 Iris (55,000 wafers) and OpenAI's Jalapeno ASIC will join the contest for supply (16 Aug, second-hand, not traced to a primary source) — a literal confirmation of this trend's claim. TSMC at OCP APAC confirmed a production yield of 98-99% for 5.5x reticle CoWoS-L, a 2028 roadmap of 14x reticle, and ten new packaging plants over three years with capacity doubling year on year, while still calling advanced packaging the largest bottleneck on AI chip shipments (expansion and bottleneck coexisting = the standing of a defining layer); Applied Materials' FY26Q3 advanced packaging business is expected to grow >70% in 2026; NVIDIA's Feynman locks in A16 + SoIC + CoWoS-L + panel-level packaging (2028H2). ⚠️ A new reliability constraint (traced to a primary source): 2.5D/3D thermo-mechanical failure and RDL electromigration are promoted to core bottlenecks, and copper (111) preferred-orientation nanotwinned structures are needed to extend life (SemiEngineering, 21 Aug) — the bottleneck keeps sinking further within the layer. |Δp|=0.02
trends.oneliner: CoWoS / SoIC / MR-MUF / hybrid bonding / glass substrates have moved from back-end supporting processes into a system-level integration and pricing-power role; packaging capability determines HBM yield, thermal management and the pace of system delivery.
trends.mechanism: The end of Dennard scaling + exponentially rising EUV cost → the marginal PPA gain from transistor scaling alone tends to zero. The reticle area ceiling + Poisson yield collapse force large chips to be recomposed as chiplets; HBM requires 2.5D packaging; in 3D stacks the DRAM junction-temperature ceiling (95°C) constrains logic-layer frequency in reverse.
trends.analogy: In urban development, "motorways and sea-crossing bridges" replace "building height" as the definer of a city's capability; construction shifts from "more floors" to "integrated structural design and building-systems integration".

trends.title: Optical interconnect reaches the rack
trends.lastLog: Held (0.79) · but a criterion defect at the trend level is registered, of the same kind as the requirement that a judgement stay neutral between implementation paths · The two legs of this trend moved in opposite directions this week, and neither move was small. The optical-interconnect axis leg strengthened: YOFC's 26Q2 net profit +1587% year on year, gross margin a record 60.5%, and cumulative hollow-core fibre deliveries above 10,000 fibre-km by mid-2026 (Nomura, 23 Aug); Innolight's 2Q26 profit beat sharply with gross margin up to 46.4% (Nomura, 24 Aug); the physical mechanism was confirmed — at 200G/lane copper still dominates the 1-2m inside a rack, but at 400G/lane the copper limit halves, Ethernet+DSP solutions fail on latency and power, and the shift to optics accelerates across racks and even within them (2026 OCP APAC); Georgia Tech's ferroelectric tuning removes the "thermal tuning stall" in optical interconnect, accelerating Mixtral 8x7B training by 2.7×. The specific CPO path leg continues to slide: Marvell CEO Matthew Murphy stated publicly that near-package optics (NPO) will reach large-scale deployment before CPO (28 Aug); Dylan Patel, on the Sequoia podcast, placed large-scale CPO deployment in the 2027-2030 range, later than the 2027-06 lock of the class A criterion here — both point the same way as the three physical bottlenecks argued at the first downgrade on 2026-08-22. ⚠️ Criterion defect registered (left for review): the title of this trend, "optical interconnect / CPO / silicon photonics as the new main battleground", is a compound proposition that binds a strengthening axis (optics displacing copper) and a sliding specific implementation path (CPO) to a single probability. When the two legs diverge, one probability can express neither the strengthening of the axis nor the slide of the path — the same underlying fault as writing one implementation path into the judgement conditions, which the standard forbids, except that here it occurs at the level of the trend title rather than at class A level. A review should consider splitting it into "optical interconnect displaces copper interconnect" (the axis) and "the timing of CPO deployment" (the path), or rewriting the title at axis level and demoting CPO to one of its confirming signals. No rewrite is made this week; 0.79 held
trends.oneliner: Copper interconnect hitting its power ceiling forces optical links to take off; CPO + silicon photonics become the necessary route to upgrading the nervous system of AI clusters, but the real master valve is InP laser supply (a 70% shortfall, geographically concentrated).
trends.mechanism: Electrical signals travelling beyond 50 cm on PCB see energy consumption rise exponentially; once in-rack bandwidth reaches the Tbps-per-lane-pair scale, the efficiency curve of electrical interfaces cannot keep up and optics becomes the only phase-continuous scalable route. But CPO co-packages the optical engine with the ASIC → overall yield = die yield × optical engine yield × optical-electrical alignment yield, and the multiplicative effect makes the early stage very painful.
trends.analogy: The medium substitutions from telegraph → telephone → fibre backbone; the 19th-century history of power transmission from DC to AC — not that DC was physically impossible, but that high-voltage AC won on engineering economics.

trends.title: 800V HVDC and wide-bandgap power
trends.lastLog: Strengthened 0.75→0.77 · the first increase after four consecutive weeks held, because this week brought both an architecture-level primary account that could be traced and the first conversion into value per unit: ① SemiEngineering, "800VDC Pushes AI Power Design From Grid to Gate" (18 Aug, traced to a primary source) + FUNDA OCP APAC — rack power density jumps from 125kW to 500kW and even 1MW, forcing a redesign of the entire transmission and distribution path from the grid to the chip gate; 48V/12V → 800VDC; the OCP frontier replaces iron-core transformers with solid-state transformers (SST) alongside SiC/GaN; PMICs are pushed down inside the DDR5 module for decentralised regulation, guarding memory data against damage from transient voltage droop. This is the first end-to-end architectural account of the trend rather than a single-device narrative. ② Mizuho estimates that Vera Rubin enters strong volume production in 2026Q4 with the platform adopting 800V DC throughout, lifting power-semiconductor value per rack from about US$15,000 to US$115,000 (7.6×) (not traced to a primary source, second-hand, sell-side estimate). ③ HexSeed Technology raised >£600,000 to convert captured CO₂ into diamond film by low-temperature microwave plasma and grow it on the surface of finished GaN devices. ⚠️ The two class B tripwires (800V adoption far below the narrative / ±400VDC continuing to dominate) drew zero signal this week; on the rule that silence = zero information, that is not recorded as confirmation. This increase rests on architectural necessity rather than adoption data, and adoption remains the weakest link in this trend. |Δp|=0.02
trends.oneliner: Once per-rack power reaches 600kW→1MW, conventional 12/48V fails physically; 800V HVDC + SiC/GaN + backside power delivery / Power Chiplet become the necessary route.
trends.mechanism: P=UI: at constant power, higher voltage means lower current, cutting copper and I²R losses sharply (voltage×16 → current÷16 → loss÷256); the traditional multi-stage AC-DC round trip loses 25-33%; Maxwell's equations set the hard constraint. Under 400A+ operating conditions on AI chips, IR-drop and electromigration push the area of power-delivery solder balls beyond the area of signal balls, forcing power delivery to give way from the front side to the back side.
trends.analogy: The 19th-century AC versus DC contest replayed in miniature inside the data centre; the evolution of electric vehicles from 12V → 48V → 800V platforms remapped onto the data centre.

trends.title: Power becomes the next hard constraint
trends.lastLog: Strengthened 0.85→0.86 · the 2027 North American AIDC power shortfall gets its first primary-source estimate (demand of about 35GW against deliverable 16.5-23.4GW, 1.8-2.1×; deliverable 2027 grid capacity is already locked up by projects that entered the queue before mid-2025; gas turbine slots are booked out to 2031; 78% of stalled projects die on permitting; over the past year 60-70% of delays are attributed to power, FUNDA, 28 Aug) + a US emergency declaration blocking some foreign grid equipment from entering the country, worsening transformer lead times (Utility Dive 828959, 27 Aug) + PJM wholesale power costs +46%. |Δp|=0.01 [Q2], deliberately small. ⚠️ The main reason for keeping the adjustment small: for the first time a competing alternative with capital behind it has appeared — Emerald AI's US$150m Series A (with NVIDIA, Siemens, RWE and JERA participating) turns data centres into second-scale flexible load and has already been deployed with NVIDIA, Oracle and Digital Realty (its "100GW released" figure is the company's own and is not treated as evidence); separately, one project developer paid £20m for grid reinforcement in exchange for interconnection — the power constraint can in part be bought with capital
trends.oneliner: Once silicon and packaging capacity catch up, the constraint moves to grid capacity, transformers (128-week lead times) and water and permitting approvals — time constants of 3-10 years, far slower than the 1-2 years of GPUs.
trends.mechanism: Grid expansion, transmission and distribution equipment manufacturing, water permits and land approvals are all limited by a triple coupling of politics, engineering and geography, with time constants of 3-10 years; GPU/HBM capacity expansion has a time constant of 1-2 years. The order-of-magnitude gap between them means the energy constraint must become visible between 2027 and 2030. Constraints of this kind cannot be accelerated with money.
trends.analogy: The "coal haulage bottleneck" of the railway age: steam engine capacity could be expanded quickly, but the capacity to move coal from mine to railhead was a product of geography and politics, and it set the real ceiling on the speed of the industrial revolution.

trends.title: Liquid cooling becomes core infrastructure
trends.lastLog: Held (0.80) · demand and institutions both strengthen, but an important correction to relative position also arrives · Strengthening: Nomura estimates global AIDC liquid-cooling penetration at 53% in 2026, approaching 60% in 2027; the Accelsius NeuCool IR150 two-phase direct-to-chip liquid-cooled rack (150kW per rack, with integrated CDU) completed its first commercial deployment at EdgeConneX in Houston (Business Wire, 27 Aug, traced to a primary source); Singapore's IMDA and Enterprise Singapore issued SS 726:2026, "Liquid Cooling Specification for Tropical Data Centres" — the world's first liquid-cooling standard for hot, humid environments, targeting a 30%+ reduction in PUE and in practice the technical entry ticket that lifts Singapore's restriction on data centre construction (institutional evidence, which this trend previously lacked); UM-Dearborn's physics-guided generative design optimises liquid-cooling channel topology inside 2.5D/3D packages, giving peak GPU temperature −33.6% and pressure drop −72.8% on a 2.7kW multi-chip package; on the demand side, front-line readings have ordinary colos receiving requests every day for racks above 100kW with water taken to the rack. ⚠️ But one correction to relative position should not be swallowed: several practitioners class cooling as "an engineering variable that can be solved through design iteration", "not absolutely unscalable, provided power and cooling are designed together from the start of a project", while listing power as the irreplaceable constraint that decides whether a project can exist at all (writing "Power. Power. Power." in a row). That is: this trend holds as critical infrastructure, but as the rate-limiting bottleneck it is weaker than T06. This does not change the trend's claim (the claim is the promotion from engineering support to critical infrastructure, and it has been confirmed), but it should stop the trend being read as a hard bottleneck of the same rank as T06, so there is no increase this week. A second related observation: 100kW+ racks depend on liquid cooling and new architectures can reach a liquid-cooled share above 90%, but CDUs, pumps, hoses and commissioning crews are becoming the new long-lead items — the thermal bottleneck has begun to migrate downstream into its own supply chain (a candidate instance of the wave migration in T01; see this week's log for T01)
trends.oneliner: Single chips >1kW plus racks >600kW make air cooling fail physically; liquid cooling goes from optional to mandatory, and traditional thermal companies are repriced by AI.
trends.mechanism: The second law of thermodynamics + a surge in point power consumption triggers a paradigm jump in thermal management. Liquid cooling caps deployment density directly — insufficient cooling capability means insufficient deployment density, and physics cannot be routed around. Because the decision is taken up front when a facility is built (low-power racks cannot be retrofitted afterwards), liquid-cooling penetration has a strong first-mover effect.
trends.analogy: The return of 1960s mainframe water cooling — historically every surge in point power consumption has triggered a paradigm jump in thermal management; analogous to the localised mechanisms of core temperature regulation in living organisms.

trends.title: Thermal limits move inside the package
trends.lastLog: Class A criterion rewritten (probability unchanged) · the original wording, "HBM4 thermal management becomes a public anxiety topic for NVIDIA / AMD", is deficient on all three dimensions: measurement — an anxiety topic is not a decidable observable; subject — it fixes on the GPU vendors, whereas thermal management is a physical constraint on HBM stacking and the parties best placed to confirm it publicly are the memory makers and the packaging houses, while GPU vendors have an incentive to play it down; outcome — the proposition becomes harder to rule the more strongly it holds (this week SK hynix gave a hard 775µm stack ceiling at Hot Chips 2026 and pushed hybrid bonding out to HBM5, so thermal management has already been quantified as the physical ceiling on HBM capacity, yet under the old criterion it could not be ruled because the party speaking was not NVIDIA/AMD). The criterion is now framed in terms of effect: the thermal constraint is publicly confirmed by ≥1 primary party (GPU vendor / HBM maker / packaging house) in the form of a quantifiable physical ceiling, and that ceiling directly limits capacity or the number of stacked layers, with technical releases / conference talks / earnings reports / official documents as the basis. Under the new criterion this week's evidence already meets the hit condition, but the collapse is not applied retroactively; it is left for the next resolution pass, once the evidence is traced to official Hot Chips material or an official SK hynix channel
trends.oneliner: Inadequate HBM thermal dissipation inside a 3D stack triggers a fatal positive feedback loop (temperature↑→refresh↑→power draw↑→higher temperature) → the compute ceiling of a chip = how much heat the more fragile memory can take.
trends.mechanism: DRAM charge retention time is exponentially sensitive to temperature (+10°C halves retention); in a 3D stack the logic layer (hot) sits directly against the DRAM layer (low temperature ceiling), so the memory layer reaches its thermal limit first and forces the logic layer to throttle back.
trends.analogy: The localised mechanisms of core temperature regulation in living organisms; deep-sea submersibles moving from whole-hull pressure resistance to local active pressure compensation.

trends.title: The bottleneck reaches materials and components
trends.lastLog: Strengthening 0.80→0.82 · bottleneck severity has triggered a supply-side capital response, a harder form of confirmation than rising prices: Linde is spending USD 1.8bn to expand ultra-pure gas capacity (USD 1.0bn in Phoenix + USD 0.8bn at Linde LienHwa in Taiwan, inferred to serve TSMC 2nm + advanced packaging) + global liquid helium supply -14% (an attack on a Qatari facility + Chinese export restrictions) + roughly 80% of InP demand tied to AI compute, producing an unprecedented shortage. Status stays at Strengthening: the class A condition, supplier order visibility ≥18 months, currently rests on sell-side research (Goldman Sachs on MLCC through 2030) rather than disclosure by the suppliers themselves, so it does not meet the collapse criterion; Linde's expansion is also a force in the opposite, easing direction, hence the deliberately small |Δp|=0.02
trends.oneliner: MLCC content per AI server board goes from 1440→10544 (+632%), PCB up 233%, tungsten up 500%; the bottleneck percolates down to the boring nodes with the lowest supply elasticity and turns them one by one into points of pricing power.
trends.mechanism: Passive component content per board in an AI server BOM is 5-20× that of consumer electronics. MLCC use changes in kind, from capacitance-driven to impedance-driven: a UWIO bus with >60,000 I/O requires the PDN target impedance to be held at very low milliohms across a wide frequency band → thousands of MLCCs of differing capacitance values working in concert; yield on high-end MLCC is only 1/6 to 1/3 of that on ordinary parts.
trends.analogy: In the 1849 California gold rush it was Levi's, selling jeans, that became the long-run winner; in the automotive chip shortage (during COVID) low-margin mature-node capacity was taken away by higher-margin AI/HPC.

trends.title: Inference and agents reshape compute
trends.lastLog: Mirror class A condition added (probability unchanged) · the first practical application of the new discipline · C46 (harness state amplification factor), created this week, is a coupling, and if its class A condition stood alone it would produce no calibration data at all when ruled — precisely the structural problem exposed by the first hard ruling on C39 the same day (eight weeks of zero rulings broken, yet still zero calibration). Under the new discipline a same-source mirror class A condition is therefore registered on this trend: identical to C46 on all three dimensions of the criterion, ruled simultaneously by the same resolving event, and when it is ruled this trend must give its probability readings before and after and enter the Brier score. The direction of the ruling is fixed in advance: state-maintenance share of tokens ≥10% → this trend's reading contains a measurable inflated component, lowered; <10% → the inflated component is engineering trivia and confidence in the reading rises. Locked to 2027-08 (the same as C46)
trends.oneliner: Compute consumption shifts from training (pulsed peaks) to 24×7 inference + agent instances, the CPU/memory/scheduling ratio reverts from 1:8 to 1:1, and the whole system design is remade.
trends.mechanism: Training = short-pulse batches + fixed weights; inference = persistent state + long-tail latency constraints + long chains of agent tool calls. The two differ almost entirely in memory bandwidth, energy-efficiency targets, network topology and scheduling system — the workload mix inverts → hardware mix, memory hierarchy and energy-efficiency optimisation are all reshuffled.
trends.analogy: From the mainframe batch-processing era to the era of distributed web servers: one-off batch jobs → a continuous stream of requests, giving rise to entirely different directions of hardware optimisation (multi-core CPU, Memcached, CDN).

trends.title: Knowledge compilation becomes a constraint
trends.lastLog: Held (0.78) · none of the positive evidence is traced to a primary source, while the negative evidence is traced and points at the amortisation assumption behind CTR itself · Positive (none traced): without structured business knowledge behind it, LLM accuracy in complex enterprise settings stalls in the unusable 60% range, rising to 90%+ once structured know-how is injected through ontology engineering; Palantir Foundry implements three levels of permission control at the semantic ontology layer, over objects, properties and cells; Action Writeback (the consistency trade-offs of writing actions back into ERP/CRM/warehouses/graph stores) is identified as the most central engineering pain point in closing the enterprise agent loop; UIUC EnSI-RAG shows quantitatively that the more material is fed in the lower the accuracy, and argues for offline preprocessing into entity-level semantic units. Negative (traced, and the most important item for this trend this week): MemTrapBench (arXiv 2608.20202), from Zhejiang University and others, demonstrates that even when the retrieved historical memory is entirely accurate and semantically relevant it induces reasoning fixation and excessive avoidance, with accuracy falling off a cliff, so an AdaptiveMem applicability-check layer must be added; NUS + Google (arXiv 2506.01265) show that piling on examples brings no substantive improvement on long-text tasks and that explicit metric guidance of the LongGuide kind is required. Implication at the pattern level: this does not negate CTR but marks out a boundary not previously modelled — the compiled artifact itself carries negative externalities, and CTR must build in a gate that asks whether it applies at this moment, otherwise the gains from pre-compilation are cancelled by the cost of fixation. A second boundary signal points the same way (an opinion, not evidence): enterprise semantic worlds drift, and the intermediate artifacts of a one-off compilation expire silently — the most dangerous moment in an ontology project is not the first modelling pass but six months later, when the business rules have changed, the original owner has left, and the agent is already making critical recommendations on the old definitions; maintenance is a long-term cost, not a one-off cost at launch. A class B tripwire should be added to this trend at review: change-management cost on enterprise semantic-layer projects is empirically shown to exceed initial modelling cost → the ROI assumption for CTR in the enterprise semantic domain needs re-estimating. Positive and negative offset, held at 0.78
trends.oneliner: Expensive runtime operations are displaced into a one-off compile step that yields structured artifacts cheap to query (KV cache pre-computation / Pinecone Nexus / Airbyte Context Store / d-Matrix SRAM weights).
trends.mechanism: The second law of thermodynamics permits local reductions in entropy — one bout of intensive compilation does the work in exchange for a low-entropy query path for downstream consumption, and marginal cost collapses. CTR is only meaningful in the range where ROI turns positive (demand frequency × data stability × compilation cost vs execution benefit), so the timing of compilation is itself a dynamic decision (an AOT↔JIT spectrum).
trends.analogy: The materialised-view pattern in databases 60 years ago / pre-compiled .lib files in EDA / consulting a formula table in a college entrance exam (derive once, look up a thousand times) / routers pre-compiling routing tables.

trends.title: The harness becomes the moat
trends.lastLog: Strengthening 0.79→0.80 · the value of a harness gets its first controlled ablation measurement: arXiv 2608.19072 (Tsinghua + Renmin University, traced to a primary source) ran a component ablation on Qwen3-1.7B-Base — an autonomous baseline of 22.0% on HumanEval vs 62.8% with the full experience framework (close to 3×), falling to 42.6% with the Evaluator removed, and down 4–8% across the board with the skill library removed. Pointing the same way: Google Cloud open-sourced its Long Horizon Harness (five defensive patterns against silent collapse over long horizons) + SemiEngineering's argument for hard guardrails + failures in 15+ independent repositories all landing in the harness layer. |Δp|=0.01 [Q1] deliberately small. ⚠️ The immediate reason for the small adjustment is that the same paper also gives a ceiling: none of the three interventions — experience framework, human intervention up front, more compute — got the policy layer to re-evaluate; across 3,557 adjacent experiment pairs the policy change rate was only 2.08%, and Evaluator suggestions at the policy layer were 0/5 rejected — a harness buys close to 3× at the execution layer but cannot buy initiative at the policy layer; Anthropic itself states that rules in context files are only a probabilistic mechanism, and that a rule which must hold should be written as hard enforcement in the manner of a Git hook. The class A condition has zero evidence and stays open
trends.oneliner: Engineering value moves from writing prompts → designing loop systems that are observable, interruptible and verifiable; the same model's pass rate goes 19%→73% under different frameworks (⚠️ pending verification: that pair of figures is not traced to a primary source; the closest public data are 42%→78%, second-hand · 2026-07-10), and the framework becomes the new moat.
trends.mechanism: An LLM call is a high-variance random variable, and a single output cannot reliably support a business process. Composing repeated calls into a self-verifying loop (plan + verify + retry + checkpoint) = turning an unreliable component into a reliable system — this is the state machine / feedback control thinking of cybernetics.
trends.analogy: The analogue operational amplifier: the gain of a single transistor is unstable, but once negative feedback is added the overall response is set by an external RC network. The framework is the negative feedback — it turns the non-linearity of a base model into a controllable system transfer function. A Boeing 737 is five orders of magnitude more reliable than a single engine.

trends.title: Engineering shifts from code to systems
trends.lastLog: Strengthening 0.78→0.80 · the role shift gets its first independent evidence at both the mechanism level and the quantitative level: ① SemiEngineering's AI engineering Amdahl's law — AI generation scales horizontally while human serial review does not, so throughput is set by the review segment, and IC engineers turn into architects and reviewers (28 Aug); ② the first observable failure mode showing why review cannot be handed to AI — models of the same lineage mass-produce vacuous or over-broad SVA assertions that pass cleanly in formal verification tools while catching no real defects (Verified. Until It Isn't); ③ arXiv 2608.19072 (traced): agents are adequate at the execution layer (mean score 10.41%→23.0%) but the policy change rate is only 2.08% and Evaluator suggestions at the policy layer were 0/5 rejected. |Δp|=0.02 [Q1]. ⚠️ Counter-evidence alongside: an enterprise withdrew its Copilot subscriptions (this hits the direction of the class B tripwire on a large-scale retreat from AI coding, but it is a single community anecdote of unknown scale, registered for observation without moving the probability) · HN puts the speed-up at only about 20%, because review ≈ writing · the productivity dividend converts first into work intensity (9–9.5 → about 12 hours). All three question net benefit rather than denying the shift itself (following the methodological line drawn on 8 Aug)
trends.oneliner: The marginal cost of code generation →0, and engineer value moves up to writing specs, setting architecture, managing agent formations and running acceptance gates; top labs hire veteran infrastructure engineers rather than PhDs.
trends.mechanism: In an automated system the value of the operator falls as automation rises, while the value of the system designer + the failure diagnostician rises at the same time. AI coding automation reproduces the industrial automation curve — the hands are replaced, the judgement is amplified.
trends.analogy: Textile workers in the industrial revolution: once the power loom arrived the spinners vanished but machinists proliferated; AI coding makes the typer vanish but brings forth the spec writer and the process engineer. After the Bell Labs era ended, top physicists flowed to new companies.

trends.title: The control plane moves to catalogs and semantics
trends.lastLog: Held (0.78) · the control-plane battlefield widened and the control plane was bypassed in the same week · Strengthening side (a wider battlefield rather than a larger share): at its 2026 conference Epic released the Ergo interface + Agent Factory (120 AI capabilities), and its structural advantage was stated explicitly as natively owning identity, permissions, patient context and the final write authority, on which basis it will eat the add-ons; the isomorphic evidence is ByteDance's Doubao Work inheriting Feishu documents, multi-dimensional tables and permission systems in one click. This extends the battlefield of the control-plane fight from the data catalog to EHR and office suites. On the capital side: Databricks closed a USD 5bn round at a USD 190bn post-money valuation (+42% on the USD 134bn of 2026-02), with ARR past USD 7bn, +80% YoY; AWS acquired DuckLabs, the commercial entity behind DuckDB (the open-source IP remains with the DuckDB Foundation and the MIT licence is unchanged; the official Amazon announcement can be traced to a primary source). Weakening side (two items, both pointing to the semantic layer not necessarily being where the value lands): ① several HN commenters judge that LLMs being good at generating SQL actually reduces the payoff from replacing SQL, that SQL will have its life extended much as assembly did, and that the people who understand the business relational model best are already SQL experts with no incentive to migrate — AI may extend the life of old standards and old catalog systems; ② discussion in r/DuckDB shows that open formats connecting systems together is no longer sufficient value, and that the new threshold is whether another long-running component can be removed. ③ A third item is an opinion: the semantic layer is necessary but not sufficient, and the durable barrier is attributed to runtime governance, the evidence loop and definitional authority inside the organisation — the last of these being an organisational asset on the customer side that cannot be captured by a vendor Catalog product. The two sides offset, held at 0.78. The class A condition (≥3 mainstream catalogs implementing interoperable queries on a public protocol, whoever initiates it) saw no new progress this week and stays open
trends.oneliner: Database competition moves up from Engine Competition to Catalog + Semantic Layer Competition (SNOW Horizon vs Databricks Unity vs AWS Glue), and data gravity migrates from storage lock-in to governance lock-in.
trends.mechanism: An agent needs to know who, why, what it may read and what it may change → data governance / permissions / approvals are productised from a manual process into an infrastructure layer. Open formats (Iceberg/Delta) weaken storage lock-in, but metadata / semantic layer / permission policy accumulate into a new governance gravity.
trends.analogy: Enterprise ERP moving up from a database melee to a fight over the authority to define business processes (SAP vs Oracle); the fight over de facto standards between Win32 API and POSIX in the OS era.

trends.title: Custom ASICs challenge general-purpose GPUs
trends.lastLog: Strengthening 0.82→0.84 · the densest week of evidence for this trend so far, and the first public benchmark in which an in-house ASIC beats the next generation of general-purpose GPU outright on energy efficiency: OpenAI's Jalapeño (700W rated / ≤550W measured, deep HBM4+SRAM integration, throughput per watt on the InferenceX benchmark 1.5–1.9× that of GB200/GB300 and end-to-end latency 1.7–3.6× lower, physical design by Broadcom, development compressed to 9–16 months, deployment in its own data centres by the end of 2026 / volume production in 2027) + the cross-section at Hot Chips 2026 (Maia 200 on 3nm ramping at year-end · 2nm started / TPU v8t · v8i / Trainium 3 in 3nm volume production / the MTIA roadmap) + JPM knocking down the rumour that TPU had been cancelled (the Broadcom-Google long-term contract runs to 2031 and locks in TPU v8–v11, with customers extended to Meta/OpenAI/Anthropic). |Δp|=0.02 [Q1]. ⚠️ Three counter-items alongside: NVIDIA acquired Groq as a low-latency disaggregated decode module for Rubin (this hits the S04 falsification keyword of a Vera Rubin counter-attack in inference; in nature it is a general-purpose vendor absorbing a specialised threat) · AWS×NVIDIA extended their agreement for 2027-28 with an additional 2 million GPUs (one company betting on Trainium 3 and on doubling its NVIDIA purchases at the same time) · SemiWiki questions Jalapeño as still in early bring-up, first light ≠ an economically competitive inference system. Alongside these, Dylan Patel's local-optimum trap sets an upper bound: uncertainty in architectural evolution means every player must keep general-purpose compute as a buffer
trends.oneliner: JPMorgan forecasts 2027 ASIC shipments of 12.5 million units (53%), passing GPU at 10.9 million units (47%) for the first time; Broadcom / Marvell hold 80%+ of high-end custom silicon; NVIDIA is not overturned, but its exclusivity in the inference segment will be eaten into.
trends.mechanism: Inference workloads converge + algorithms stabilise → the PPA gains from hardware specialisation far outweigh the loss of flexibility (2.7× compute per dollar / 1.02× compute per watt). Cloud vendors hold the full software stack + enormous demand of their own + enormous capital, so the TCO advantage of an in-house ASIC overwhelms the GPU.
trends.analogy: The car industry moving from the general-purpose V8 engine to purpose-built hybrid electric motors: once commuting / urban duty cycles converged, the combined efficiency of a dedicated motor + battery system far exceeded that of a general-purpose internal combustion engine.

trends.title: Model convergence drives price compression
trends.lastLog: Held (0.78) · second consecutive week held, and a criterion defect in the composite claim, shared with T04, is registered · The two legs of this trend moved in opposite directions again this week. The capability-convergence leg strengthened, and its form rises for the first time to a "structural rebasing": Harvey (legal AI, valued at about $11 billion, serving roughly 3/4 of the top US law firms) dropped GPT and post-trained its own Tenet on open-source Kimi K3 (2.8T), bringing running cost down to 1/4 of a mainstream general-purpose base model; Cursor (valued at about $60 billion) likewise built in-house on the open Kimi base; Thomson Reuters' Thomson-1 started from Qwen3.5-397B/Qwen3.6-35B, with about $40 million invested over two years but only about $450,000 for a single full training run, matching or slightly exceeding Sonnet 5 / GPT-5.5 on specific legal tasks (the Thomson Reuters press release on the company's own site is traced to a primary source). Three vertical leaders in the $10 billion class switching their base to open weights in the same period is the strongest set of evidence this leg has produced to date. The price-collapse leg continues to reverse: DeepSeek's fourfold price increase for V4 took effect on 08-16; this week DeepSeek, Zhipu, Alibaba, Tencent and Baidu raised API prices together; Zhipu's open release of GLM-5.3 (744B) drops MIT for a restrictive licence (MaaS giants with more than $10 billion of total revenue over 12 consecutive months must pass a safety review before commercial use) — "open-source" has turned from unconditional public benefit into a targeted defensive moat, a new kind of reversal mechanism for the price-collapse leg. ⚠️ Criterion defect registered (left for review · same origin as T04 but more serious): this trend is a composite claim joining "model capability convergence" and "open vs closed-source price collapse", yet the three consecutive downgrades of 2026-08-01 / 08-08 / 08-15 were all driven by the price-collapse leg alone, while the convergence leg strengthened throughout. The current 0.78 therefore represents neither the convergence leg nor the price leg, and has lost the relative comparability the rules require. The recommendation at review is to split it into two independent trends. No rewrite this week; 0.78 held. Class A (whether a second leading vendor publicly applies time-of-day / peak-off-peak / congestion pricing to a flagship inference model before 2026-09-16) gained strong directional evidence this week but has not yet expired: ① the initiator, DeepSeek, withdrew its all-day weekend peak price of its own accord (a partial rollback); ② followers used uniform price increases rather than time-of-day pricing — an independent search confirmed that Qwen3.8 Max ($2/$6), GLM and Kimi are all on flat rates or subscription tiers, none of them implementing peak-off-peak pricing. On the explicit class A criterion ("time-of-day / peak-off-peak / congestion pricing", not the broader "API price increase" of the watch-keywords), the strong current tendency is towards failure. With only 2 and a half weeks to the lock point, the next resolution pass must rule on it
trends.oneliner: DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / Doubao 2.1 Pro close in on Claude Opus / GPT-5.5 at 1-15% of the price, and the industry shifts from "which model is strongest" to "who controls the context pipe".
trends.mechanism: Training algorithms + data + architecture are so homogeneous that frontier capability must converge mathematically; differentiation can arise only in proprietary data / feedback loops / systems integration. Once model weights are open they cannot be locked down again, and the speed of diffusion is set by network effects.
trends.analogy: Linux's comeback against Windows: commercial value migrated from "the operating system itself" to "services built on the operating system", and open-source crushed the capital barrier of closed-source with zero marginal cost + global collaboration. AI model weights are moving along the same path, from "closed-source core asset" to "infrastructure commodity".

trends.title: AI capital splits around bottlenecks and debt
trends.lastLog: Held (0.84) · the debt leg hardened, the pricing-power leg diverged, and the two offset; class A scores its first half-hit · The debt-paradox leg is at its strongest this week: an S&P Global Ratings feature — capex at the six largest hyperscalers rising from about $870 billion in 2026 to more than $1.3 trillion in 2027, free operating cash flow (FOCF) turning negative in both the 2026 and 2027 financial years and unable to turn positive before 2029, financing shifting to long-dated debt, equity pledges, finance leases, off-balance-sheet JVs with sovereign funds and energy consortia, SPVs and residual-value guarantees, and S&P explicitly warning that off-balance-sheet structures make conventional credit analysis extremely difficult (08-27); US AI-related corporate debt issuance year to date in 2026 is about $220 billion vs $12.5 billion in the same period last year; Broadcom is in talks over a $60–100 billion off-balance-sheet SPV debt package, and its 5-year CDS has jumped from 40bp in May to a new high of 120bp; since mid-August investment-grade buyers have demanded higher premiums on new technology issues, and technology-sector spreads have widened against the broad market to a rare degree. ⚡ Class A half-hit (no collapse): the class A condition as rewritten on 08-22 requires ≥2 bottleneck links with price increases already realised whose leading holders show a 2× year-on-year market capitalisation. The price-increase leg hits hard this week and does so across ≥2 links — memory (16Gb DDR4 spot +879% YoY, 2027 HBM contract prices expected +70–140%, spot fill rate <50% and moving into allocation) and complete systems (NVIDIA notifying CSPs of 15–17% price increases on Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin); the 2× year-on-year market-capitalisation leg has no data point at all this week, and no source gave market-cap multiples for the three memory majors. Under the rule that a single leg of a compound condition does not collapse it (following the T06 precedent of 2026-08-08), it stays open. A reverse reading on the pricing-power leg appeared at the same time, and happens to validate the 08-22 criterion rewrite once more: Marvell's non-GAAP operating margin of 36.6% vs NVDA 66% / AVGO 67%, GAAP EPS only 1/3 of non-GAAP, and a slight beat still met with an after-hours fall — among the named companies the price takers continue to be squeezed from both ends; SOX is down 22.8% from its 52-week high and into a technical bear market, and semiconductor ETF SMH saw a record $2.8 billion of outflows in August while QQQ took in $10.9 billion. The two legs offset; 0.84 maintained
trends.oneliner: The market punishes the middle of the chain that issues debt to expand capex (Oracle / CoreWeave) and rewards bottleneck holders (SK Hynix / Lattice / Arm / Kioxia / Tower); closed-source labs race to IPO and compute is being securitised (Apollo $35 billion / Broadcom $29 billion guaranteeing Anthropic).
trends.mechanism: Rational capital rewards the links with positive marginal cash flow and the least elastic supply. When every link in the AI chain is forced to expand but only the bottleneck nodes can raise prices → capital must split; meanwhile the players stuck in the middle are forced to turn future cash flow into assets (IPO / compute securitisation) to hold up liquidity. The swelling scale of AI infrastructure financing is turning some chipmakers from "chip suppliers" into "financial guarantors of AI infrastructure deployment".
trends.analogy: The 1849 California gold rush: miners lost money on average while the railways (capacity bottleneck), the shovel sellers (equipment bottleneck) and the banks (capital bottleneck) took 90% of the gains. The AI "debt paradox" is the miners' version of that script. And the contagion mechanism of guarantee chains in the 2008 subprime crisis.

trends.title: AI becomes a sovereign asset
trends.lastLog: Raised 0.82→0.84 · last week's new dimension was "sovereign actors extending from states to companies"; this week's new dimension is that sovereign instruments extend from export controls (restricting outflows) to foreign-investment security review (unwinding an inflow deal already completed), with the first fully executed precedent. ① China's NDRC ordered the unwinding of Meta's $2 billion acquisition of Manus under the Measures for the Security Review of Foreign Investment (ruled 2026-04-27; this week the unwinding was executed in full, Manus resumed independent operation, Tencent is in talks to become the largest strategic shareholder after the separation, and all user data accumulated in Meta's accounts and servers since the acquisition date had to be physically deleted on 08-23/24) (NPR / CNBC 2026-04-27~28; legal analyses from Morgan Lewis, O'Melveny and Trivium China). Three underlying implications: (a) this is the first public confirmation that a cross-border AI deal has been unwound through the foreign-investment security review mechanism, using neither antitrust nor export controls; (b) Manus had redomiciled to Singapore in 2025-06 and the acquisition closed in 2025-12, yet the regulator still reached through — an explicit declaration that redomiciling grants no exemption so long as core technology, founders or research infrastructure originate in or remain tied to mainland China; (c) the target was neither chips nor weights but an agent product with autonomous operating capability plus its team, extending sovereign leverage to "ownership of talent and algorithms". ② Sovereign compute takes physical form: Firebird AI's Hrazdan AI compute factory in Armenia entered service (phase one $500 million, NVIDIA DSX reference architecture + Dell PowerEdge, >6000 B200, 15–18MW; planned expansion to 300MW and >70,000 Rubin/Blackwell by the end of 2027, targeting the largest sovereign AI infrastructure in the CIS; Armenia's prime minister and Jensen Huang attended) (PR Newswire / Dell 08-08). ③ Article 50 of the EU AI Act took effect, and from 2026-08-02 Anthropic embeds an invisible machine-detectable watermark in all text from new Claude models and adds C2PA to images and files (12/13 Aug, second-hand, not traced to a primary source, treated as directional only and not as the main basis for Δp). ⚠️ Hedges: the main evidence (Manus) was ruled in 2026-04 and this week only completed execution, which is delayed discovery rather than a new event this week, so it is priced at 0.02; Apple's mainland China Macs adding Tongyi Qianwen (cannot be traced to a primary source, second-hand) is not counted in Δp; the 77-institution joint letter on open weights / the OSAA counter-move still show no new progress this week (silence = zero information). |Δp|=0.02
trends.oneliner: Fable 5 blocked → AI models / materials / EDA / specialty gases are all upgraded to export-controlled goods; open-source + domestic stacks become the hedge, and the technology stack forks by region.
trends.mechanism: When a technology materially affects military, economic and information productivity, the state inevitably intervenes — the pattern repeated historically with atomic energy, cryptography and semiconductors. AI has all three properties at once, so its conversion into a sovereign asset is a question of when, not "whether". Open weights cannot be recalled → producing a coexistence of "controlled closed-source frontier + unstoppable open-source".
trends.analogy: Cold War nuclear controls: enrichment technology was governed by the NPT framework, but the diffusion of reactor designs could not be stopped, and the outcome was "observable blocs". AI is forming an isomorphic pattern.

trends.title: Embodied AI moves from demos to work
trends.lastLog: ⚡ Second downgrade 0.71→0.69 · the first full test week after the "applicable scenario" dimension was locked in on 08-22, and that criterion was measured directly by a source traced to a primary source, with a negative reading: ChinAI #372, "China's overhyped embodied AI" — some leading domestic vendors draw 70%+ of revenue from the research market, relying on related-party transactions with local state-owned enterprises and on university research equipment purchases, with no industrial-grade closed loop (folding a towel not finished in 15 minutes, picking up a bearing in 70 seconds); a second independent origin cross-confirms it: >91% of humanoid revenue comes from research, education and commercial consumer uses, with productive uses only 2.7%–4.5% (not traced to a primary source); and paradigm-level doubt comes for the first time from an establishment authority (Wang Jian of Zhejiang Lab: the VLA generalisation bottleneck, real data collection of only a few hundred samples per person per day), aimed squarely at the mechanism assumption that the data flywheel dominates. |Δp|=0.02 [Q1]. ⚠️ There is no shortage of positive evidence but none of it fits the 08-22 scenario criterion (Robot Era's 1,200–2,000 units/hour with no revenue broken out · Dogotix's $900 million raise and plan for 1,000 units a month are not operating revenue · Science Robotics is academic) — for a second consecutive week the criterion does the work of blocking a raise. Status stays Strengthening (the class A lock runs to 2027-06 and has not expired, the class B tripwire has not been hit, and no formal downgrade trigger fires), but with two consecutive weeks of negative direction, a downgrade to Loosening should be considered at the next test week if there is still no positive reading that fits the criterion
trends.oneliner: Capital and industry consensus has moved from "robot backflips" to "pharmacy picking / AMR operations / closed-loop VLA scenarios", emphasising the data flywheel + constrained-scenario deployment + on-device chip stacks; on-device / automotive / industrial are the scenarios that really take off, and humanoids are only the entry point.
trends.mechanism: The embodied "perceive-decide-act" loop has to close in milliseconds, at low power, under constrained compute. The bottleneck met by large-model routes such as VLA is "the absence of a sustainable data flywheel" — physical interaction data cannot be gathered at the scale of internet text and depends on deployment in real settings + iteration fed back from it. That means whoever first makes a constrained scenario work gets the positive data feedback.
trends.analogy: The route split in autonomous driving between "L5 in one leap" and "incremental L2+ + scenario focus": the real winners are those who deploy at scale in constrained settings (motorways, campuses) and accumulate a data flywheel, not those chasing general capability.

trends.title: China's chip stack joins up
trends.lastLog: Held (0.79) · this week brought the strongest candidate evidence for "a joined-up chain" this trend has seen to date, but because it rests on a single origin and on vendor-side figures it falls into Q3, registered for verification with no adjustment · [pending verification] Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash consumed trillions of tokens in a week of anonymous testing on OpenCode / OpenRouter (23.2T in the first 6 days on OpenRouter, taking roughly a 20% weekly token share during the anonymous period), and that high-concurrency production traffic was reportedly carried entirely by about 100,000 domestic AI chips (Huawei / Hygon / Moore Threads), with not a single NVIDIA card; Zhipu worked with SGLang to rebuild the inference engine for domestic chips (EPD encode-prefill-decode disaggregated scheduling, W8A8 mixed-precision cache quantisation, tensor parallelism), giving 3× end-to-end serving performance and levelling per-token compute cost with mainstream NVIDIA GPUs (27 Aug, figures are vendor-side, single origin, not traced to a primary source). Why this would matter if true: the claim of this trend is a move "from point breakthroughs to a joined-up chain", and all previous evidence has been single points (one tool qualified, one line's yield, one vendor's revenue); this one is a complete closed loop of chip + inference engine + model + real production traffic, and its evidential level is higher than any single-point yield figure. Why no adjustment is made on it this week: the only source is a vendor-side figure relayed by an account, with no third-party cross-confirmation (OpenRouter's official usage page, an independent benchmarking body, a chipmaker announcement); a Q3 reading calls for no adjustment this week, registration in the pending-verification queue, and a further attempt to trace it next week. It has been registered for observation, and the missing check is public OpenRouter usage data or independent third-party confirmation of "zero NVIDIA in the serving fleet". Regular strengthening evidence that fits the criterion this week (not enough to move the number on its own): YMTC's 2026Q1 revenue of RMB 48.219 billion and net profit of RMB 36.710 billion, the establishment of YMTC Phase III with registered capital of RMB 20.72 billion, a controlling stake in packaging and test house Hongmao Micro, and a $4.9 billion IPO filing; AMEC's 26Q2 operating profit +351.1% year on year, CCP high-aspect-ratio etch at >90% yield on memory lines, tungsten deposition revenue +220% year on year in 2025, and a plan to cover about 70% of advanced packaging equipment steps within 3–5 years (Bernstein 08-22) — all of it broker commentary, not traced to a primary source
trends.oneliner: DeepSeek completed V4-Pro post-training on Ascend 910C (≥1000 units, with V4 optimised for Ascend) + ACM Research's in-house mini-line + AMEC's acquisition of Hwatsing to fill the CMP gap + Hygon's deployments in financial-sector settings + Beijing IC manufacturing +82.5% in the first 5 months — equipment + CPU + materials break through in parallel, and domestic substitution moves from "usable" to "good to use".
trends.mechanism: Domestic substitution in chokepoint links follows an "engineering decomposition" logic: any "high-threshold" problem can be broken into small sub-problems attacked in parallel, drawing on a dividend of 5 million STEM engineers + a home market as a trial-and-error runway + materials sovereignty (rare earths / gallium / germanium) + the capital coordination of the Big Fund. This is the "ants gnawing a bone" path in which engineering scale grinds down a technology gap.
trends.analogy: China's high-speed rail moving from importing and absorbing to indigenous innovation along an engineering path: standardised technology + large-scale domestic demand + sustained engineering investment, ending in comprehensive superiority in trainsets / control systems / track construction and other links.

couplings.title: T10 (inference paradigm) → T02 (HBM / bandwidth takeover)
couplings.cause: Continuous agent inference + KV cache growing multiplicatively along five dimensions (length / depth / breadth / duration / persistence) → HBM / bandwidth demand surges.
couplings.mechanism: Inference tokens ↑ → KV cache swells (8192 tokens versus 512 tokens: KV cache capacity grows linearly, ≈16×; cumulative HBM read traffic across a full generation ≈256× — producing each token requires a linear scan of the entire existing KV cache) → HBM capacity / bandwidth demand ↑ → Samsung / SK Hynix / Micron lock up 20%+ of DRAM capacity under long-term contracts.

couplings.title: T02 (HBM) → T03 (CoWoS tightness)
couplings.cause: HBM must be paired with CoWoS advanced packaging → CoWoS capacity becomes the slowest link → the pace of the entire AI compute expansion chain is set there.
couplings.mechanism: HBM and the GPU / ASIC die share a silicon interposer → CoWoS 2.5D packaging is mandatory → expanding monthly CoWoS capacity takes 18-24 months (far longer than HBM's own capacity ramp) → even with HBM capacity in place, CoWoS holds the chain back.

couplings.title: T03 (CoWoS) → T01 (bottleneck conservation, reverse feedback)
couplings.cause: Packaging capacity that takes 18-24 months to expand becomes the bottleneck of the whole chain → AI model scaling is forced to slow → the chain forms a closed loop (preventing the chain from extending indefinitely)
couplings.mechanism: CoWoS capacity cannot be expanded in the short term → actual AI chip deliveries are capped → the growth curve of training compute bends → inference demand growth is limited from the supply side → the demand pull in C01 is constrained in reverse.

couplings.title: T02 (HBM as a strategic asset) → T09 (run on commodity DRAM) → consumer electronics price increases
couplings.cause: The HBM wafer conversion ratio rises with each generation + long-term contracts lock up capacity → spot prices for commodity DRAM outside LTA protection spike → Apple / Xbox raise prices → demand destruction in consumer electronics (a 13-year low)
couplings.mechanism: HBM's share of DRAM wafer capacity goes from 19% → 28% (2025 → 2027; TrendForce 2026-06 official criterion: 18% / 22% / 30% for 2025/26/27 · vintage difference) → commodity DRAM unit prices double YoY → memory's share of PC / handset BOM cost jumps from 11% to 51% → Apple's Cook raises prices for the "first time in 40 years" → consumer price elasticity is triggered → demand destruction.

couplings.title: T03 (CoWoS) → T19/T09 (valuation jump for chokepoint holders + materials bottleneck)
couplings.cause: The packaging value chain transmits to PDFS/Onto/CAMT/Aehr + specialty gases / molybdenum / copper-fill electroplating chemicals
couplings.mechanism: CoWoS expansion → demand for TGV laser etching + copper-fill electroplating + RDL + inspection and metrology ↑ → chemical consumables / equipment / data toll-booths benefit in step → the real moat sits in the 6-12 month qualification stickiness of chemical consumables (the deepest moats often belong to the supporting materials).

couplings.title: T04 (CPO co-packaging) → T03 (packaging yield multiplication)
couplings.cause: CPO co-packages the optical engine with the ASIC → overall yield = die yield × optical engine yield × optical-electrical alignment yield → the early stage is very painful
couplings.mechanism: The CPO volume production timetable is governed by the packaging yield curve rather than by the optical devices themselves. Any CPO shipment timetable has to be judged against the packaging line; early on, die yield 95% × optical engine yield 80% × alignment yield 70% = 53% overall → not economically viable.

couplings.title: T01 (GPU supply catches up) → T06 (power becomes the new bottleneck)
couplings.cause: Silicon and packaging are in place → data centres move from "nowhere to put it" to "no power to run it" → power infrastructure becomes the new hard bottleneck
couplings.mechanism: GPU / HBM / CoWoS capacity expansion lands in 2027-2028 → the data centre build bottleneck is no longer silicon → grid capacity + transformers (128-week lead time) + water and permitting approvals become the new constraints → time constants of 3-10 years, far slower than the 1-2 years of silicon capacity expansion.

couplings.title: T05 (800V HVDC) → T07 (liquid cooling synergy + rack redesign)
couplings.cause: 1MW per rack requires liquid cooling + a full rack redesign; 800V distribution + liquid cooling + rack-level power management form a system-level coupling
couplings.mechanism: 800V HVDC lifts rack power density to 1MW+ → liquid cooling becomes mandatory (air cooling fails physically) → in-rack power, thermal management and interconnect are redesigned; liquid cooling in turn lowers system pressure drop → pushing rack power density higher still.

couplings.title: T01 (the bottleneck moves downstream) → T20 (geopolitical leverage migrates with the bottleneck)
couplings.cause: The further downstream the node, the higher its geographic concentration (JP specialty gases, NL lithography, US EDA, KR HBM, CN rare earths / MLCC) → it naturally becomes an export-control weapon
couplings.mechanism: As the bottleneck moves down into materials / equipment / specialty processes → the geographic concentration of the node rises → governments place it on strategic materials lists → export controls + long-arm jurisdiction are turned into instruments.

couplings.title: pattern substrate-spectrum (deep specialisation of dynamics silicon) → T03 (glass substrates / hybrid bonding + multi-material packaging)
couplings.cause: Power Chiplet / Computing-with-Dynamics require new heterogeneous integration packaging formats (multi-material CTE matching + 3D co-design)
couplings.mechanism: Deep specialisation of dynamics silicon / optical computing / analogue silicon → chiplets of different materials (SiC + GaN + Si + magnetics) have to be packaged together → multi-material CTE matching + thermal co-design + 1kW/cm³ physical density → glass substrates + hybrid bonding are the necessary path.

couplings.title: T10 (agent adoption) → T11 (CTR / Context Store turned into artifacts)
couplings.cause: Agent fan-out call frequency ↑ → the ROI of pre-ETL + pre-indexing turns positive → enterprise data systems migrate from federated calls to pre-compiled artifacts
couplings.mechanism: Agent cost per query = number of calls × API unit price + token cost; once query frequency passes the critical point, pre-compilation ROI turns positive (the CTR pattern made concrete). Locality Crisis Ring 3 pushes to the threshold at which data must be held locally.

couplings.title: T18 (model commoditisation) → T12 (frameworks / loops become the new moat)
couplings.cause: Once foundation models homogenise, differentiation is only available at the system layer (same model, different frameworks: pass rate 19% → 73% — ⚠️ pending verification: this pair of figures has not been traced to a primary source; the closest public data is 42% → 78%, second-hand · 2026-07-10)
couplings.mechanism: DeepSeek at 1% of the cost + GLM-5.2 open-sourced the same day → the closed-source premium is compressed → value shifts from renting models to framework design + proprietary context pipelines + feedback data. Capability Surplus unfolding across the AI tool stack.

couplings.title: T12 (Loop Engineering) → T13 (the engineer's role becomes spec writer)
couplings.cause: People step back from inside the loop to outside it → value concentrates in setting goals + designing verification gates + diagnosing system failures
couplings.mechanism: Loop / Harness Engineering spreads → the value of engineers writing code by hand ↓ while the value of system design and failure diagnosis ↑. The industrial automation curve replayed in AI coding: hands are replaced, judgement is amplified.

couplings.title: pattern verifier-bound (verifier maturity) → the speed of AI breakthroughs in a given field
couplings.cause: The strength or weakness of the verifier directly determines whether AI can crack a field at scale, and how fast
couplings.mechanism: The capability ceiling of a neural network = search within the boundary of the verifier; a weak verifier → the model only learns statistical shortcuts (reward hacking); a strong verifier → compute expansion can converge on real structure.

couplings.title: T18+T20 (open-source acceleration + Fable 5 export controls) → T14 (MCP multi-vendor abstraction)
couplings.cause: The commercial risk of closed-source dependence becomes visible → engineering accelerates MCP standardisation to keep vendors hot-swappable
couplings.mechanism: Anthropic Mythos falls under export controls because of its cyber capabilities → buyers recognise that dependence on a single closed-source vendor is a commercial risk → GLM-5.2, open-sourced the same day, is read as a substitutable anchor → engineering pushes MCP into a protocol standard (what USB-C is to hardware, what TCP/IP is to networking).

couplings.title: T10 (agents as digital employees) → collapse of SaaS per-seat pricing
couplings.cause: Agents replace human seats by completing tasks → the SaaS anchor of "how many people are using it" stops working → software companies acquire AI capability (Salesforce's 3.6 billion acquisition of Fin)
couplings.mechanism: Traditional SaaS marginal cost ≈ 0; token marginal cost + usage scale ∝ exponential cost growth. AI is promoted from "feature plug-in" to "digital employee" → the pricing anchor moves from "seat licence" to "settlement per task".

couplings.title: T10 (agent adoption) → class B work friction ↑ (governance/audit/lineage)
couplings.cause: Automated agent decisions ↑ → demand for after-the-fact attribution / audit / compliance / explainability ↑ (incompressible, and in fact expanding)
couplings.mechanism: An agent cannot bear legal liability → after-the-fact attribution / audit / compliance checks / dual-signature processes are required; the more agents are deployed, the greater the supervision friction; this is the Friction Duality pattern confirming itself in enterprise AI deployment.

couplings.cause: Value migrates from the consumption side to the artifact production side → self-produced scarce data assets (PDFS / in-house benchmarks / neutral process pools) become a new kind of toll-booth
couplings.mechanism: The CTR pattern displaces value from "runtime consumption" to "compile-time production". The production side holds the right to manufacture artifacts → customers buy access rather than ownership → a moat that compounds over time (30 years of the PDFS Characterization Vehicle).

couplings.title: T15 (ASIC shipments overtake GPU) → dilution of CUDA exclusivity in the inference segment
couplings.cause: Inference is cost-sensitive and its use cases are fragmented, so it moves to multiple hardware platforms first; NVDA is not overturned, but its exclusivity in the inference segment is eaten into
couplings.mechanism: Inference workloads converge → the ROI of hardware specialisation ↑; cloud providers + in-house silicon at the model developers + open-source software stacks (Modular MAX / Mojo / ROCm) stack up on three tracks → CUDA is squeezed in the inference segment.
